content: I, who am called by this name,May all sentient beings always take refuge in the Guru, take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, and take refuge in the Sangha.Homage to the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha, Śākyamuni. Homage to the Tathāgata Vajragarbhapramardin. Homage to the Tathāgata Ratnarcis. Homage to the Tathāgata Nāgeśvararāja. Homage to the Tathāgata Vīrasena. Homage to the Tathāgata Śrīnananda. Homage to the Tathāgata Ratnāgni. Homage to the Tathāgata Ratnacandraprabha. Homage to the Tathāgata Amoghadarśin. Homage to the Tathāgata Ratnacandra. Homage to the Tathāgata Vimala. Homage to the Tathāgata Śrīdatta. Homage to the Tathāgata Brahmadeva. Homage to the Tathāgata Brahmadatta. Homage to the Tathāgata Varuṇa. Homage to the Tathāgata Varuṇadeva. Homage to the Tathāgata Śrībhadra. Homage to the Tathāgata Candanaśrī. Homage to the Tathāgata Anantaujas. Homage to the Tathāgata Prabhāśrī. Homage to the Tathāgata Aśokaśrī. Homage to the Tathāgata Arthadarśin. Homage to the Tathāgata Puṣpaśrī. Homage to the Tathāgata Brahmavikrīḍitābhijña. Homage to the Tathāgata Padmavikrīḍitābhijña. Homage to the Tathāgata Dhanaśrī. Homage to the Tathāgata Smṛtiśrī. Homage to the Tathāgata Parikīrtitaśrī. Homage to the Tathāgata Indraketudhvajarāja. Homage to the Tathāgata Suvikrāntaśrī. Homage to the Tathāgata Yuddhajayavikrānta. Homage to the Tathāgata Vikrāntagāmin. Homage to the Tathāgata Samantāvabhāsavyūhaśrī. Homage to the Tathāgata Ratnapadmavikrāntin. Homage to the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha, Ratnapadmasupratiṣṭhitaśailarāja.May all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and perfectly complete Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who reside, live, and remain in all the world-systems of the ten directions, please turn their attention to me. In this life and in all my births throughout beginningless cyclic existence, whatever sinful actions I have committed, caused others to commit, or rejoiced in; whatever property of the stūpas, the Saṅgha, or the Saṅgha of the ten directions I have stolen, caused to be stolen, or rejoiced in stealing; whatever five actions of immediate retribution I have committed, caused to be committed, or rejoiced in; whatever paths of the ten non-virtuous actions I have engaged in, caused others to engage in, or rejoiced in; and whatever karmic obscurations I have accumulated that would cause me to go to the hells, the animal realm, or the realm of hungry ghosts, or to be born in a remote border region, or as a barbarian, or among the long-lived gods, or to have impaired sense faculties, or to hold wrong views, or to fail to please the Buddhas when they appear—all such karmic obscurations, in the presence of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who have become primordial wisdom, who have become the eye, who have become witnesses, who have become valid authorities, and who know and see, I confess, I disclose, I do not conceal, and I do not hide; and from now on, I shall refrain from and restrain myself from them. May all those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, please turn their attention to me.Whatever roots of virtue I have acquired in this life and throughout beginningless lives while wandering in samsara—even by giving a single mouthful of food to a being born in the animal realm—and whatever roots of virtue I have acquired from observing ethical discipline, from abiding in celibate purity, from fully ripening sentient beings, from generating the mind of supreme awakening, and from unsurpassed pristine wisdom, I gather, assemble, and combine all of these together, and I dedicate them fully to the unsurpassed, supreme, and perfect awakening, which is the highest of the high and the greatest of the great.Just as the past Buddha Bhagavans have fully dedicated, and just as the future Buddha Bhagavans will fully dedicate, and just as the present Buddha Bhagavans are fully dedicating, so too do I fully dedicate.I confess each and every sin. I rejoice in all merit. I exhort and pray to all the Buddhas. May I attain the supreme and holy unsurpassed pristine wisdom.To the supreme among humans, the Victors who dwell in the present,Those who have passed away, and likewise those yet to come,To all those whose praised qualities are like a boundless ocean,I join my palms and go for refuge.This concludes the Noble Mahāyāna Sūtra entitled "The Heap of Three."
